anomalies.observed: Anode A2 (D30 pin 4) of the dual LED sits on ESTOP_OUT, and its cathode K2 (pin 2) goes through R60 back to ESTOP_OUT. Both ends of that LED channel therefore land on the same ESTOP_OUT net, so the channel cannot conduct. The companion channel is wired the expected way: anode A1 (pin 3) on /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV, cathode K1 via R59 to GND.
anomalies.expected: Channel 2 should mirror channel 1: its anode should be on the switched 3.3 V LED supply (/LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV), with its cathode driven through R60 to ESTOP_OUT as the status signal.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The E-stop status LED channel in D30 never lights, so the operator gets no indication of the ESTOP_OUT state from that LED.

anomalies.observed: D2 (red LED) has its anode on the open-drain output U27.4 (Y) and its cathode through R31 to GND. U27's input A (pin 2) is tied to +5V. Every other U-driven indicator (D1, D12, D17) uses the anode on a supply rail and the cathode on the buffer output, so the LED is oriented opposite to the rest of the design.
anomalies.expected: With an open-drain SN74LVC1G07 output that has no pull-up, the indicator should have its anode on the supply and its cathode on the output, so that pulling the output low lights the LED.
anomalies.impact: The red indicator behind U27 probably cannot be driven on or off as intended; it stays dark because the open-drain output cannot source current to the anode.

parsed.summary: The most likely deviation is in the dual-LED channel D30, where anode A2 is tied to ESTOP_OUT rather than the switched LED supply, so that channel cannot light. A secondary, lower-confidence concern is the reversed orientation of D2 relative to the other buffer-driven indicators.
